subject: Urgent: Streaming degradation affecting chat/streaming endpoints — mitigation & follow-up
body:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Felicia Gomez <felicia.gomez@storico.ai>, Marco Alvarez <marco.alvarez@storico.ai>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial alert: streaming/chat degradation impacting responses (investigating)

Hi Felicia / Marco,

I'm writing to let you know we detected elevated streaming latencies for chat endpoints used by Storico.ai starting ~07:45 PDT this morning. Some streams are experiencing token delays and intermittent stalls; non-streaming (batch/generate) requests remain within normal latency bands for most traffic.

We’ve already pulled in SRE and the runtime team and are treating this as a P2 incident. Current asks for you:
- For critical user flows, consider switching streaming calls to the non-streaming endpoint (stream=false) temporarily — this will return complete responses rather than partial streaming tokens and should avoid the stall behavior.
- If you need help with a quick toggle, Grace and I can coordinate.

We’ll follow up within 90 minutes with a root-cause update and recommended mitigations. Our apologies for the disruption — we know this impacts conversational experiences.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0142

From: Felicia Gomez <felicia.gomez@storico.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Marco Alvarez <marco.alvarez@storico.ai>, Support Team <support@storico.ai>
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 08:29:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial alert: streaming/chat degradation impacting responses (investigating)

Thanks Jordan — we’re seeing it in production as well (multiple users reporting long pauses while streaming). Our web client is heavily optimized for streaming; switching to non-streaming will degrade UX but we can do it for a short window.

Can you tell us whether this is tied to a specific region or model variant? Also — is there any ETA for mitigations?

Felicia
Head of Product, Storico.ai

---

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 08:55:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial alert: streaming/chat degradation impacting responses (investigating)

Jordan / Grace — updating the thread with technical summary and immediate mitigations we pushed: 

Summary (what we see):
- Onset: ~07:40 PDT; increased token emission latency and client-side stalls for streaming endpoints across multiple GPU pools in us-west-2.
- Root cause (preliminary): A recent kernel selection change combined with a spike in long-context chat sessions caused the runtime's continuous-batching queue to favor larger batch windows; that amplified per-token serialization delays for low-throughput streams.

Immediate mitigation actions already taken by runtime team:
- Rolled back the kernel selection heuristic change (deployed 08:20 PDT) which restored baseline kernel paths for short/latency-sensitive streams.
- Temporarily tightened the batching window for streaming-only queues to reduce per-token aggregation delays.
- Enabled a low-latency model variant (quantized int8) for specific model families to reduce kernel latency for streaming.

Customer-facing mitigations we recommend and how we can help you implement them: 
1) Quick client change (recommended if you need fast, guaranteed responses):
   - Switch streaming->non-streaming (stream=false) for critical requests. Example curl:
     curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate" -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" -d '{"model":"rwd-llama-2.1", "input":"<...>", "stream": false}'
   - This avoids token-level stalls at the expense of progressive UX.

2) Reduced chunking and token cap (moderate effort, low risk):
   - Reduce client chunk_size to 64 tokens and set max_tokens to 512 for conversation requests while we stabilize. This reduces the window for aggregation-induced delays.

3) Region/variant routing (short-term):
   - Route critical sessions to our us-east-1 region or to the low-latency quantized variant we turned on. We can provide routing TTLs and an API flag: "prefer_region=us-east-1" or "model_variant=compact-low-latency".

What to expect next:
- We rolled the rollback and batching changes at 08:20; telemetry shows improvements but we’ll continue monitoring through the day.
- If your production traffic is sensitive, Grace and I can coordinate a rolling traffic shift and perform smoke tests.

Diego (SRE) — will follow up with logs and traces for Storico.ai sessions to confirm whether the rollback removed stalls for their keys.

Evelyn
Senior Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime

---

From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Felicia Gomez <felicia.gomez@storico.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 21 May 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Final update + post-incident notes and recommended config (postmortem attached)

Hi Felicia / Marco — thanks for the patience. Following up with final findings and actionable guidance. The attached postmortem includes timelines, impact graphs, and actions taken; key points below: 

Root cause (final):
- A recent heuristic update intended to optimize throughput for long sequences incorrectly increased the batching threshold for streaming queues. Under the traffic spike of many long conversations, this produced larger batch windows and increased per-token latency for low-volume streams.

Impact:
- Affected customers: ~8 enterprise customers in us-west-2 with heavy streaming usage; Storico.ai saw 12-18% of streaming sessions exhibit 3–15s token stalls.
- Duration: ~07:40 PDT — 09:05 PDT (rollback + stabilizing tuning completed by 09:05; residual edge cases resolved by 10:30).

Remediation & follow-ups we completed: 
- Reverted the kernel selection heuristic and shipped a safer gating rule to prevent it from affecting streaming queues without explicit long-context signals.
- Implemented a temporary cap on streaming batch window size (persisted for 72 hours while longer-term tuning is validated).
- Enabled a low-latency quantized model variant for affected model families as an automated fallback.
- Added additional telemetry and an alert that triggers when streaming token emission latency exceeds 500ms for >1% of sessions in a region.

Recommended customer configuration (we included a small playbook in the attached mitigation file):
- If you cannot tolerate streaming stalls, set stream=false on mission-critical endpoints for the next 48 hours.
- As an alternative: keep streaming enabled but set max_tokens to <=512 and chunk_size=64 until we complete validation (this preserves much of the streaming UX with lower stall risk).
- Use the model_variant flag to opt your traffic into the low-latency quantized fallback: model_variant=compact-low-latency.

Support & credits:
- We will apply a one-time service credit equivalent to 10% of May streaming usage for impacted customers as a gesture of goodwill; Grace will coordinate credit process for Storico.ai.

Attachments included:
- redwood-streaming-incident-postmortem-20260521.pdf (timeline, telemetry, RCA)
- mitigation-playbook-commands.txt (curl snippets, SDK toggles, routing flags)

If you’d like, we can schedule a 30-min runbook walkthrough and coordinate staged traffic tests to validate your changes — Grace and I are available tomorrow morning.

Thanks again for flagging this quickly; please reply here if you want us to perform the toggle for your keys.

—
Diego Fernandez
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
diego.fernandez@redwood.com

Grace will send the credit paperwork and coordinate the internal billing request. Thank you for moving quickly — we’ll continue to monitor and keep you posted.

Best,
